children.game_version: The Barn Players: Children form a circle mimicking the Wang Tepus barn, taking turns playing the royal court while others match the rhythmic kecerek clapping and arm swings.

avoid: Abrupt pivots or unsupported weight shifts
seniors.counts: Simple 4-count or 8-count cycles matching the basic rebana pulse.
seniors.seated_version: Perform the Bertabik arm motions while seated firmly on a stable chair, swinging arms gently forward, backward, up, and down in time with the percussion.
seniors.standing_version: Perform basic upper-body swinging from a stationary standing position with feet planted shoulder-width apart without sudden foot shifts.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce the arc of arm swings to mid-torso height at a moderate, comfortable cadence.

feedback_rules.description: Differentiate unornamented, direct arm swinging from stylized royal classical hand flourishes.

learning_units.description: Execute the Bertabik opening choral movement, focusing on rhythmic to-and-fro arm swinging.
Perform vertical up-and-down arm swings synchronized with the percussive strikes of the rebana and kecerek.

prerequisites.description: Upper-body mobility and shoulder endurance sufficient for sustained swinging gestures.

social_formats.description: Staged in an open barn setting with a cast of fifteen to twenty performers surrounded in the round by village spectators.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Abbreviated, crude, and vigorous swinging motions moving forward, backward, upward, and downward.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Staged centrally within an open barn with spectators enclosing the playing space.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Primarily standing level; jumps not described in sources.
movement_profile.partnering: Group choreographies and dialogic exchanges between royal characters, shamans, and chorus.
movement_profile.posture: Upright village theatre stance facilitating continuous arm mobility.

signature_moves.description: Rhythmic horizontal swinging of both arms forward and backward during vocal chants.
signature_moves.name: To-and-fro arm swing

signature_moves.description: Vertical swinging gesture highlighting punctuation from the kecerek and rebana.
signature_moves.name: Up-and-down arm swing

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Direct, lively, and punctuated by percussion strikes.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid excessive or fluid wrist flourishes typical of court classical styles; Mek Mulung arm mechanics are direct and abbreviated.

music_profile.musical_form: Begins with the Bertabuh simultaneous overture, followed by Bertabik choral song, interspersed with pantun poetic exchanges.
music_profile.sound_description: A sharp, clattering percussive foundation dominated by the rhythmic snapping of kecerek concussion sticks and resonance of rebana drums, underscored by deep gong strokes. Piercing above this percussive wall is the reedy, sustained contour of a single small oboe, accompanied by unornamented syllabic group singing.
music_profile.vocal_style: Syllabic vocal delivery with minimal ornamentation, sung directly by the instrumental musicians.

basic_steps: Bertabuh: Await the opening simultaneous percussion roll.
Bertabik: Group vocalization with coordinated forward and backward arm swinging.
Ayunan Lengan: Up-and-down rhythmic swinging of the arms while standing in place.
Pantun transition: Pausing dance motion to engage in alternating poetic recitation.
teaching.formation: Open barn layout with fifteen to twenty performers surrounded by seated spectators.
teaching.level_notes: Beginners concentrate on synchronizing basic arm swings with the percussive meter before learning specific choreographies such as Tarian Sembah.
teaching.rhythm: Percussive tempo driven by rebana, kecerek concussion clappers, and gongs; specific meter not described in sources.
